title.analysis: 'Every Level' promises a comprehensive progression after a recognizable windfall. Clear lottery topic but no jackpot amount or secrecy puzzle, unlike PLgVQhvtU_A's $600M and 'Nobody Knows'; the actual progression is a single decline rather than selectable wealth levels.
title.script_alignment: Opening invokes an uncited 70% ruined-winner statistic, then places viewer three days from payday with $1,143 and a winning $2 ticket. Sacramento cash-option paperwork reduces $450M to $141.75M; mother's mortgage and Casey's debt create emotional generosity before Reggie's Raptor/second request tests boundaries. Miami mansion, staff and background-check date convert freedom into isolation. Seven-year jump brings illiquidity, $15M collateral loan, 25% crash, $8M call and $2.8M tax demand; warehouse return and Casey's couch close the loop. Objects and callbacks maintain coherence through escalation, but long consecutive losses and little alternate choice make downfall predetermined. Ending trails into 'Oh. Oh.' and audio completeness is unverified.

script.claim_audit: 70% bankruptcy claim lacks cited study. California FAQ retrieved October 17 says winner identity public, contradicting blind-trust anonymity; not an archived July capture. $225M less 24% equals $171M and flat 37% yields $141.75M, but marginal-tax simplification and fixed 50% cash value are assumptions. $300K monthly burn for seven years totals $25.2M, not enough alone to reconcile $100.75M net-worth loss; other spending unquantified. Portfolio composition/collateral threshold cannot derive $8M call after 25% fall. House bought outright yet foreclosure arrives without identified house-secured debt or tax-lien process. Casey debt switches credit-card to student loans. November crash seven years after win is fictional future plot, not July 2026 market event. No real winner/address ownership verified; IRS negotiation and gift enforceability statements not validated.
